findings.text: reckon/serve.py:1290 computes watch._snapshot_reuse_key(pointer) immediately after calling watch._watch_snapshot(pointer, ...) at :1279, and that function computes the same key itself (reckon/crew/recovery_watch.py:1334). Every live run's whole classification composition is therefore stat'd twice on every roadmap read, doubling the per-run cost of the live-run readings on the read path this section exists to make cheap. Recovery_watch.py is inside section 50's declared write paths, so returning the key _watch_snapshot already took was available.

The clock case asserts measured['recomposed'] > DOCUMENT_COUNT, and its cover rests on the live-run state being carried in the snapshot key (reckon/serve.py:1284 and :1294), because _watch_snapshot re-derives that state at the passed moment. The read path it claims to guard does not refresh clock-derived readings: reckon/serve.py:1366-1397 returns a stored payload on an exact key match with no re-derivation, so section 50's declared negative control for this case, returning the stored snapshot on a key match without the refresh, cannot turn the case red. Any regression in that refresh would be invisible to the case, and the case's first assertion (line 662) is computed through serve._roadmap_live_readings itself, so it does not exercise the roadmap read at all.

The final manifest records after_suite (c22ec0def, 0 failures) but carries no baseline_suite, which its own as-delivered attempt-2 manifest did at line 15. A promotion reader is therefore left to pair the repaired head against a base arm it cannot find in the record, and added_failure_count cannot be derived mechanically from the pair; the base arm log itself (base-gate.log, 39 passed, EXIT=0) is still named under test_logs, so the facts survive but the field does not.
